definitions.explanation: safety barriers installed at train platform edges that open and close in sync with train doors

examples.english: This station has platform screen doors.

examples.japanese: ホームドア⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦{設置|せっち}→設置：09750_secchi⟧⟦されて→する：00392_suru⟧⟦{安全|あんぜん}→安全：01131_anzen⟧になった。
examples.english: It became safer after the platform doors were installed.

examples.japanese: ホームドア⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{前|まえ}→前：02255_mae⟧⟦で→で：00502_de⟧⟦{電車|でんしゃ}→電車：00522_densha⟧⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{待|ま}って→待つ：00469_matsu⟧⟦ください→下さい：02899_kudasai⟧。
examples.english: Please wait for the train in front of the platform doors.

notes:
ETYMOLOGY:
From English "home" (platform) + "door"
Also called ⟦{可動式|かどうしき}→可動式：27179_kadoushiki⟧⟦ホーム→ホーム：00113_hoomu⟧⟦{柵|さく}→柵：13103_saku⟧ (movable platform barrier)

PURPOSE:
- Prevent falls onto tracks
- Prevent suicides
- Reduce train delays from accidents
- Keep platform climate-controlled (in some stations)

TYPES:
- Full-height type (フルスクリーンタイプ) - floor to ceiling
- Half-height type ({腰高|こしだか}⟦タイプ→タイプ：01534_taipu⟧) - waist height

SPREAD:
- Major cities are gradually installing them
- Required for new construction
- Retrofitting older stations is expensive

RELATED WORDS:
- ⟦{人身事故|じんしんじこ}→人身事故：08475_jinshinjiko⟧ - train accident involving a person
- {転落防止|てんらくぼうし} - fall prevention
